note: Captured once from the published effect-dynamodb@1.40.0 and @effect-dynamodb/schema@1.40.0, installed outside the repo and run by a scratch script against DynamoDB Local. Entities Plain and Retained (versioned: { retain: true }) over { id, n?: number, counts: Record<string, number> }, counts configured { storedAs: SparseMap(), field: 'sr' }, on DynamoSchema.make({ name: 'sr', version: 1 }). Each case starts from a row holding the map whole (put { id: 'a', n: 10, counts: { a: 1 } }), as entries (put with counts {}, then a raw UpdateItem SET counts#a = 1 REMOVE sr), or both (the whole-map put, then a raw SET counts#a = 7), and sends one update copying an entry into n (pathSet or pathSubtract with isPath), standalone or in Transaction.transactWrite. Recorded: its outcome (a result, or a failure's tag and the first line of its message), every request it sent, whole and in order, every row of the table after it, and what get read back. The table's name is replaced by <table>, UUIDs by <token> and timestamps by <time>. Never regenerate it: it is the record of what 1.40.0 did.
